proof_summary: From the defining sum one obtains \(a(n+1)=(2^n-1)a(n)+2^{\binom{n+1}{2}}\); for an odd prime, Fermat’s theorem and \(\binom{n+2(p-1)+1}{2}-\binom{n+1}{2}=(p-1)(2n+2(p-1)+1)\) make both recurrence terms invariant under the shift, while the shifted base value is forced to equal \(a(1)=1\), so induction applies. For \(p=2\), the recurrence directly shows every \(a(n)\) with \(n\ge1\) is odd.
